fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. Matthew says Mary "…was found to be with child through the Holy Spirit." (Matthew 1:18). Later the angel says it again, that the One conceived in her "…is from the Holy Spirit." (Matthew 1:20). Same source both times.

Zechariah is a priest (Luke 1:5), and Luke tells us he and his wife Elizabeth were going to have a son named John (Luke 1:13). That's a different story, friend. In Matthew's account, the text says Mary was found with child "…through the Holy Spirit." (Matthew 1:18). Easy to mix up when there are so many baby announcements going around.

Elijah was a prophet (1 Kings 18:36), but he's not in this passage at all. Matthew 1:18 says Mary "…was found to be with child through the Holy Spirit." No prophet, no priest, just the Holy Spirit. I once mixed up a sprinkle jar with a salt jar, so I'm not judging.

Nice guess, but the temple courts aren't in this scene. The text says the angel "…appeared to him in a dream…" (Matthew 1:20). The message came to Joseph in a dream, and the text doesn't mention the temple.
Fields aren't in this scene, friend. Matthew 1:20 says the angel of the Lord "…appeared to him in a dream…" The dream is where the message came.

Yes, baker. Joseph had resolved to divorce Mary quietly, but the angel says, "…do not be afraid to embrace Mary as your wife…" (Matthew 1:20). The angel gives the reason too: the One conceived in her "…is from the Holy Spirit." So the angel doesn't tell him to go ahead. He tells him to embrace Mary as his wife.

You got it, baker. The angel says, "…you are to give Him the name Jesus, because He will save His people from their sins." (Matthew 1:21). The reason for the name is right there in the same sentence. That's what the name is about, straight from the angel.

A widow is someone with a story of her own in the Bible, like Naomi in the book of Ruth (Ruth 1:3). But the prophet's words here say, "Behold, the virgin will be with child and will give birth to a son…" (Matthew 1:23). The word is virgin, friend. Good thing you can check it.

Queen has a royal ring to it, and Jesus does come from the family of David the king (Matthew 1:1). But the prophet's words don't use that word. They say, "Behold, the virgin will be with child and will give birth to a son…" (Matthew 1:23). Fancy title, but not the word in the verse.
That one has a nice ring to it, but it's not what Matthew says. He tells us Immanuel means "God with us…" (Matthew 1:23). The meaning is given right there in the verse.

That's a nice meaning, but it isn't the one Matthew gives. What matters here is that Matthew tells us what Immanuel means: "God with us…" (Matthew 1:23). He gives the meaning right in the verse. No guessing needed.

Not here, friend. Joseph's earlier plan was to divorce her quietly (Matthew 1:19), but after the dream, the text says he "…embraced Mary as his wife." (Matthew 1:24). Matthew doesn't mention anyone being sent away.
